text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hassan to preside over a series of religious talks in Rabat on the occasion of the holy Moslem month of Ramadan.
- Interior Minister Driss Basri says a convention of partnership between the government and the deputies is necessary to solve social problems of Casablanca city.
- Third economic and social Euro-Mediterranean summit to be held in Morocco in November.
- The government warns Islamist students at the university of Casablanca. Story refers to students' recent disturbances and demonstrations on the university campus.
- Morocco expects an exceptional harvest of olives in 1996/97 season.
- Three Moslem fundamentalist students to appear before a tribunal in Casablanca for "disturbing public order".
- To be efficient, Morocco's telecommunications sector needs urgent upgrading.
- Prices of pharmaceutical products are expected to be gradually liberalised.
